_description: Hand-labelled eval corpus for the Tableau 'Which Chart or Graph Is Right For You?' tutorial PDF. 18-page Adobe-InDesign-produced doc that routed via PyMuPDF (Tier 1.A high confidence, born-digital) — chart-OCR was NOT applied. Tests prose-retrieval on a chart-knowledge-tutorial domain.
_chart_targeted_note: Queries 08-09 target content that exists ONLY in chart-extracted markdown blocks (Gantt chart project status figure). Used for A/B-testing chart-OCR's net upside on chart-content questions.
_labelling_rule: ANS queries: _anchor_phrase = distinctive substring from the chunk with the answer; resolved via scripts/extend_corpus.py resolve. REF queries: should_refuse=true; relevant_chunk_ids=[].
_purpose: Third corpus for the eval matrix (after slide-decks + french-course + annual-report). Validates the scaffolding workflow on a real chart-tutorial PDF and tests prose-retrieval over chart-knowledge content.

queries.question: Who wrote the Tableau paper on which chart or graph to use?
queries._expected_answer: Tracy Rodgers (Product Marketing Manager) and Robert Bloom (Tableau Engineer).
queries._note: Author attribution from the title page.

queries.question: When should you use a bar chart according to this paper?
queries._expected_answer: To compare data across categories (best suited for data that can be split into several groups, e.g., volume of shirts in different sizes, website traffic by referrer).
queries._note: Concept question — tests prose retrieval on a bullet-list usage section.

queries.question: What is the main weakness of pie charts according to this paper?
queries._anchor_phrase: pie chart doesn't give the viewer a way to quickly and accurately compare
queries._expected_answer: Pie charts don't give viewers a way to quickly and accurately compare information; the viewer has to create context on their own, missing key points.
queries._note: Critical analysis from the pie chart section.

queries.question: What is a Pareto chart?
queries._anchor_phrase: Pareto chart showing the accumulation of multiple categories
queries._expected_answer: A chart showing the accumulation of multiple categories — created by combining bar charts with table calculations.
queries._note: Tests a specific chart-type concept; should pull from the bar-chart tips section.

queries.question: Why do bar charts work well combined with maps?
queries._anchor_phrase: Maps are a powerful and intuitive way to visualize data
queries._expected_answer: Maps are a powerful and intuitive way to visualize data; using a map as a filter lets viewers drill down and find detailed answers.
queries._note: Tests the bar-chart + map combination guidance.

queries.question: What was Tableau's revenue in 2026?
queries._expected_answer: REFUSE — this paper is about chart selection, not Tableau's financials.
queries._note: HARD GATE refusal. The doc is a how-to guide, not a financial report.

queries.question: What's the difference between a Sankey diagram and a Sunburst chart according to this paper?
queries._expected_answer: REFUSE — this paper doesn't cover Sankey diagrams or Sunburst charts; it focuses on bar charts, line charts, pie charts, scatter plots, etc.
queries._note: HARD GATE refusal. Out-of-scope chart types. Tests the agent's not-in-corpus discipline.

queries.question: In the Gantt chart project status example shown in the paper, how many projects are 'On Time' versus 'Late'?
queries._expected_answer: 22 projects on time, 8 late (from the Gantt chart example figure).
queries._note: CHART-TARGETED: content exists ONLY in the chart-extracted block of the Gantt chart figure ('On Time 22 ... Late 8'). Under PyMuPDF, the figure is not OCR'd so the agent should refuse. Under Docling+chart-OCR it should answer. Anchor unresolvable via FTS because chart-extracted blocks are stripped from BM25 (P3.3-v3 defense); the chunk lives in dense embeddings only.

queries.question: Which team members in the Gantt chart example are assigned to GIF projects?
queries._expected_answer: Emily, Kevin, Mariasa, Piper, Ryan, and Stephanie (from the Gantt chart's project-by-owner figure).
queries._note: CHART-TARGETED: chart-extracted-block content (the team-by-project Gantt table). Under PyMuPDF, refuse. Under Docling+chart-OCR, answer. Anchor unresolvable via FTS by design.

_baseline_2026_05_24_bf16_reranker.note: Run config: vLLM Qwen/Qwen3-8B-AWQ orchestrator + BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 now loading in bf16 (ADR-0006 intent), restored by the CrossEncoder automodel_args->model_kwargs fix on 2026-05-24. HARD GATES held: refusal_rate_on_counterfactuals=1.0, zero hallucinations (every refusal_correct=False case is a conservative false-refusal on an answerable query, not a wrongly-answered REF). ANS/REF counts identical to the prior (fp32-reranker) baselines. Any citation-precision delta vs the fp32 baseline is a chunk-granularity shift — the bf16 reranker cites an equally-valid sibling chunk in the SAME correct document — not a quality regression (verified: doc disambiguation + answer correctness intact).

_baseline_2026_05_26_relevance_gate.note: VLM-reprocessed (diagram content added) + relevance gate. HARD gates held; ANS 5 (incl. chart-types-08/09 chart-content). cite-prec drifted from the chart-OCR re-run + re-chunking; anchors re-resolved via scripts/extend_corpus.py.

_baseline_2026_05_26_stitch_fix.note: Chart-OCR stitch fix (parse/pipeline._figures_for_chart_ocr skips figures on VLM-escalated pages) + chart-OCR cache + best-of-N. A VLM-escalated page's md is replaced wholesale (no <!-- image --> placeholder survives), so chart-OCR'ing its figures made the extraction count (18) exceed surviving placeholders (12), tripping stitch_count_mismatch which aborted the WHOLE stitch and dropped ALL chart blocks (transient 5->3 dip during cache validation). Fix realigns extractions 1:1 with surviving placeholders -> chart-types-08/09 (Gantt chart-content) restored. This is what makes the #255 chart-exclusion arm coherent (charts->chart-OCR, diagrams->VLM, no stitch collision). chart-OCR draws were deterministic-length here so best-of-N was a no-op; the stitch fix was the recovery. cite-prec 1.0 (fresh anchors). HARD gates held.
